title: Seattle University seal-and-signature lockup — a third party's registered trademark
note: THE SECOND ARTIFACT THIS SITE REPRODUCES RATHER THAN CITES, and the first one that belongs to somebody else. art:hero-photo asks "where did this picture come from". This record asks a different question with a harder answer: "are we allowed to show this at all". It was opened on 2026-09-03 while moving the nav to sit over the hero photograph, because the design question (a black mark cannot be seen on a dark picture) turned out to sit downstream of a permission question nobody had asked. WHAT THE FILE ACTUALLY IS. public/brand/seattle_university_logo.png is not the Seattle University wordmark. Rendered on white it is the ringed academic seal — eagle, shield, IHS monogram, 1891 banner — followed by the SEATTLE UNIVERSITY wordmark. The 2024 brand guidelines name that exact composite "SEATTLE UNIVERSITY SEAL AND SIGNATURE" (p.17) and put the seal in the most restricted tier the document has. public/brand/seattle_university_seal.png is the same seal standing alone. So BOTH marks this repo ships are the academic seal, and the component's `variant` prop was offering a choice between two forms of the same restricted mark. WHY THIS IS pending-owner AND NOT blocked. Three published rules point the same way — the seal is "not intended for general use" and its use outside four named offices is "not permitted"; any SU trademark needs "prior, expressed, written permission from Marketing Communications"; and the licensed-content policy names "Web sites and pages (commercial and personal)" among the uses that require it. That is a strong signal and it is still not a finding of fact about THIS site: the owner may hold a permission this repo has never seen, and the university itself says fair use is a question for counsel rather than for the FAQ. `blocked` would also delete the asset out from under public/docs/business_card_design.html and two other legacy pages that reference it, and C15 would turn the build red for work nobody had agreed to. So the record states the doubt at full strength and the SHIPPING CHOICE IS MADE SAFE UNDER IT INSTEAD: components/ui/Mark.tsx reads this status and renders the affiliation as TEXT until it says "verified", so the mark reaches no page in either nav state, plated or not. Flip one field here and the raster returns; nothing else has to change. Setting the affiliation in words is not a workaround — naming an institution to state a true fact about yourself reproduces no mark, and it is the same argument Mark.tsx already made for the College of Science and Engineering sub-brand.

openQuestions: Do you hold written permission from Seattle University Marketing Communications (brand@seattleu.edu) to display a university mark on duyng-portfolio.com? Their licensing FAQ says any SU trademark "may not be used without prior, expressed, written permission from Marketing Communications", and their licensed-content policy names "Web sites and pages (commercial and personal)" among the uses that require it. If you do, paste it and this record closes as verified.

Are you aware that public/brand/seattle_university_logo.png is the ACADEMIC SEAL plus the wordmark, not the wordmark alone? The 2024 guidelines reserve the seal for Commencement, diplomas and official communications and say its use by anyone outside the offices of the President, Provost, Deans, Board of Trustees and official staff "is not permitted". If we ever get to show a mark here, the wordmark or the SU interlock is the mark to ask for — the university encourages community use of the interlock — and neither is in this repo.

If Marketing Communications approves a mark, ask them in the same message for the WHITE / reverse lockup and for permission to place it over a photograph. We could not verify a reverse variant from the public web: the asset library sits behind the Redhawk Hub login. Note that the wordmark's approved colours are red, black and white, so a white wordmark is ordinary — but the seal carries "Do not alter or attempt to recreate these elements in any way", so recolouring the seal is not ours to do even to white, and the isolation rule (p.16) says no "typography, rules or photography" may enter a clear-space margin one full logo-height wide, which a mark sitting on the hero photograph does by construction.

public/docs/business_card_design.html, public/docs/business_card_print_ready_FedEx.html and public/docs/index_business_card.html all render this same file on a printed business card. That is a different use from site chrome and this territory did not touch it. Should it be re-cut with the affiliation set in type as well, or does it fall under a permission you already hold?

provenance.note: THE MEASUREMENT, kept here so nobody re-opens the design argument without it. The wordmark half of the file is pure #000000 on transparency — sampled every second pixel, 100% of opaque pixels right of x=156 sit below luminance 60, and the mean is 0. The nav sits on the hero's CREST, where components/site/hero-scrim.module.css paints an effective scrim alpha of 0.2500 full width (the 0.8656 column only starts after the ease, 18px above the first glyph). Compositing the shipped hero variants under that 25% veil and measuring the worst pixel inside a 28px lockup box at the wrap's left gutter: 1600x900 1.04:1, 1280x800 1.04:1, 861x1000 2.33:1, 390x844 2.38:1, 375x812 2.38:1. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a graphical object. The mark fails at every viewport, and fails worst on desktop, because at 1280 and 1600 the gutter is the dark ivy arch. A white plate would fix the ratio and is the treatment the guidelines imply — but at the guidelines' own isolation width (one full logo height, p.16) a 28px lockup needs an 84px-tall plate, which is taller than the bar, and the owner has spent seven rounds removing exactly that white rectangle from the top of this photograph. Neither arm is available, which is what sent this to the permission question in the first place.

title: DUY NGUYEN / PROVABLE AI lockup — the site author's own brand mark
note: THE THIRD ARTIFACT THIS SITE REPRODUCES RATHER THAN CITES, and the first one that is arguably the owner's own. art:hero-photo asked "where did this picture come from". art:su-mark asked "are we allowed to show this at all". This record asks the question that sits between them and is the easiest of the three to skip: "whose work is this, and what is the small line under it promising?" It was opened on 2026-09-03, the day public/brand/logo-source.png appeared in the working tree, because an intro animation was about to put this mark on the first frame every visitor sees. WHAT THE FILE ACTUALLY IS, MEASURED. 2046x769 RGBA PNG, 228,158 bytes, sha256 877b7813906640f564337a5972a680d4b13c3f55db73ae02914a8ecd526f6f06 — byte-identical to public/brand/personal_brand.png, which is the same image under an earlier name; both are listed in sourcePaths so deleting either does not blind C15. 93.8% of sampled pixels are fully transparent (alpha 0), so the mark composites over a photograph without a plate — which is the single fact that makes the owner's blurred-hero requirement buildable at all, and it is worth stating plainly because the reference implementation's .mp4 could not have done it. Ink occupies x 155-1884, y 221-528 of the 2046x769 frame: roughly 20% transparent margin on every side, so a renderer that fits the raw PNG to a box gets a mark 20% smaller than it looks. THERE IS NO VECTOR MASTER. No .svg and no .pdf are on disk, so any inline-SVG reveal is a TRACING of this raster, and a tracing is a derivative work — which is a rights question rather than a technique question, and it is why openQuestion 6 exists. THE TWO COLOURS, MEASURED AGAINST THE SITE'S OWN TOKENS. Cream is #F2DBBC (modal opaque value, consistent across the monogram, the wordmark and the N). Crimson is #8D131B. The site's accent token is --color-crimson #AA0000. These are NOT interchangeable, and globals.css already anticipated exactly this question and answered it for a different hex: rule 5 permits swapping in #A2192B precisely because L(#AA0000)=0.085460 and L(#A2192B)=0.085511 are identical to two decimals, so no ratio in the file changes. That argument does not extend here. L(#8D131B)=0.062076, 27% darker; on the ink ground it is 1.93:1 against the token's 2.34:1, and on paper 8.98:1 against 7.43:1. So the mark introduces a SECOND RED to a palette whose rule 4 states there is exactly one accent — permissible for a logotype, which is not a token, and a thing to decide on purpose rather than discover later. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS FOR THE INTRO. Sampling public/brand/hero/hero-soft-l.webp (the baked blur the reveal plays over) in the central band where a lockup would sit: the cream reads 10.94:1 at the median ground and 5.21:1 at its brightest, strong everywhere. The crimson reads 1.57:1 at the median and 1.34:1 at its brightest — effectively invisible. The consequence is worth stating without softening it: for the whole duration of the reveal the reader sees DUY NGUYEN and does not see PROVABLE AI. That is not a WCAG failure (SC 1.4.3 exempts logotype text — src:wcag-logotype-exemption), and it is not nothing either. Two honest readings, and both are available: the line the record is least sure about is also the line the reader cannot make out, which is either a lucky accident or an argument for setting the tagline on the paper ground where it measures 8.98:1 and can be read and judged. WHY disclosureRequired IS false WHILE THIS IS PENDING. It is a placeholder, not a verdict, and the schema forces the choice: attributionRequired is three-valued so a pending record can decline to answer it, but disclosureRequired is a plain boolean with no null. false matches the only precedent (art:su-mark, also pending-owner) and it must be revisited the moment openQuestion 1 comes back — if the answer is that the mark was AI-generated, the page owes a line by exactly the argument art:hero-photo already made, and this field is then wrong. RECORDED SO IT CANNOT BE FORGOTTEN.

openQuestions: WHO MADE THIS MARK? Four answers, four different records, and nothing may be said about the mark's origin on any surface until one of them is on paper: (a) you designed it yourself; (b) you commissioned a designer; (c) you generated it with an AI tool; (d) it came from a logo-maker or a purchased template. Answer (c) is the one that changes what the page owes a reader — this site already discloses that its background image is an AI-generated composite, and a mark generated the same way and shipped silently would be the same omission in a more prominent place.

HEADS-UP FOR WHOEVER RECORDS THE ANSWER: if it is (a), your own design, the corpus currently CANNOT record it. provenance.origin's enum is unknown | owner-photograph | institutional-asset | licensed-stock | ai-generated | ai-generated-composite | third-party. There is no value for a work the owner authored that is not a photograph, and 'owner-photograph' would be a false statement about a drawn lockup. The schema needs a value such as 'owner-original' before the most likely answer can be written down. This record stays 'unknown' in the meantime, which is honest but is not a substitute for the fix.

IF IT WAS COMMISSIONED OR PURCHASED: what does the licence actually grant? Three things specifically — commercial use, the right to modify (an intro that animates the mark in pieces is a modification), and whether the designer or marketplace retains any rights or requires credit. If a designer holds copyright and granted only display rights, tracing the raster into inline SVG and animating the strokes is a derivative work that the licence may not cover.

WHOSE TYPEFACE IS THE WORDMARK SET IN? This is the rights question that gets missed. DUY NGUYEN is set in a specific high-contrast serif, and a great many display and licensed serifs — including most webfont and desktop licences — either forbid logo use outright or require a separate, paid logo/embedding licence. If you or your designer set this from a font, we need the font's name and the licence it was used under. If it was drawn as lettering rather than typed, say so and this question closes for good.

THE TAGLINE — this is a judgement call and it is yours, not the corpus's. 'PROVABLE AI' is the line under your name. On a business card nobody would look at it twice. Here it lands about one scroll above a band that reads 'every limit is quoted from that record rather than paraphrased around it', on a page that retracted a misattributed 90% figure and that voluntarily discloses its own hero image as synthetic. In that specific neighbourhood a careful reader can take 'provable' literally — as a claim that the work carries proofs — and the page does not deliver that. It delivers sourced claims and stated limits, which is a different thing and, honestly, a stronger one. MY READ: it is a slogan, not a claim, and it stays a slogan for exactly as long as it is set as a logotype and never repeated as a sentence. Three options: (1) keep it and change nothing; (2) keep it, and hold the rule that no surface and no agent may gloss it, expand it, or use the word 'provable' in prose, so it stays a name; (3) change the line. I would take (2) — it costs nothing, it keeps your mark, and it closes the one failure mode I can actually name: the agent asked 'what does Provable AI mean?' and answering with a capability claim nobody sourced. Note that this page has already retracted a claim of precisely that shape — ret:duy-integral-theorem, a 'proof' that nothing supported — which is why this is being raised rather than left alone. lib/corpus/brand.ts implements option (2) today; if you pick (1) or (3), that file changes.

THE SECOND RED, AND THE MISSING VECTOR. The mark's crimson is #8D131B; the site's accent is #AA0000. They are not interchangeable — globals.css rule 5 permits a swap only for a hex of identical luminance, and this one is 27% darker. Do you want the mark recoloured to the site token so the page carries one accent, or does the mark keep its own crimson as a logotype exempt from the palette rule? Related, and needed either way: there is no .svg or .pdf master on disk, only the PNG. If you have the vector original, drop it at public/brand/logo-source.svg — otherwise the reveal has to be traced from the raster, which is lower fidelity and, depending on the answer to question 1, a derivative work.

provenance.note: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE TWO MARKS, recorded here because it is the thing that goes wrong silently. From the moment the intro ships, this page carries two institutional-looking marks: the Seattle University affiliation in the nav, and this personal lockup on the first frame. The nav's affiliation is TEXT and not a raster, because art:su-mark is pending-owner and components/ui/Mark.tsx reads that status — so the two marks are never actually adjacent as artwork, and that is a happy accident of an unrelated permission question rather than a design anyone chose. It should not be relied on. If art:su-mark ever flips to verified and the seal returns to the nav, a university trademark and a personal brand mark will sit in the same viewport, and 'PROVABLE AI' under a name beside a university seal reads as an institutional programme to a reader who is not looking closely. affiliationStatement above is the standing sentence for that case and it is grounded in clm:msds-enrolment, so no surface can upgrade 'student' into anything warmer: the record it would have to cite says student. The corpus was checked on 2026-09-03 for language already reading that way and is clean — the only endorsement-adjacent string in the new surfaces is the footer's, which the rebuild had already removed and documented ('© 2025 Seattle University. All rights reserved.' asserted a copyright the university does not hold). ONE COORDINATION FACT, RECORDED BECAUSE GETTING IT WRONG SILENCES THE GATE. assetDir is public/brand/logo — the directory scripts/gen-logo.mjs actually writes, not the public/brand/intro this record first guessed at from the reference implementation's layout. The difference is not cosmetic: C15's assetsOnDisk() stats this exact path, so a wrong assetDir means thirteen derived renditions ship while the provenance warning stays quiet, which is the failure mode where a gate looks green because it is looking at nothing. sourcePaths additionally lists public/brand/personal_brand.png, which the generator does not read; it is the same bytes under the earlier name, and listing it means deleting either copy cannot blind the check.
